paragraphs: On Thursday, Ranger Mark came to the school library. He brought four big pictures from the national park. Each picture had a caption and three key words. The Explorers wanted to put them on the library wall. May asked the questions. Lily wrote the answers. "A good caption is short," said Ranger Mark, "and key words are the best words for the picture."

Picture one showed a small green frog. The caption said, "A frog sits among green leaves." The key words were frog, leaves, and green. "Why is the word among good?" asked May. "It shows that the frog is in the middle of many leaves," said Ranger Mark. "You cannot see the frog fast." "It is the same color as the leaves."

Picture two showed an insect on a flower. Its wings were thin and yellow, and they moved a little in the wind. The caption said, "A wild insect rests on a yellow flower." The key words were insect, wild, and flower. "Is the insect a butterfly?" asked Lily. "Yes, it is a butterfly," said Ranger Mark. "The word wild tells us that nobody owns this creature." "A wild creature lives in nature and finds its own food."

Picture three was dark. It showed the forest at night. The caption said, "The night walk begins at seven o'clock." The key words were night, walk, and forest. Ranger Mark stood in the picture with a small light in his hand. "Visitors begin the night walk at the park gate," he said. "We go slowly, and we listen to the sounds." May wrote the three key words on a card.

The final picture showed a green nature kit on a table. The caption said, "A nature kit has a notebook, a pencil, and a bottle of water." The key words were kit, notebook, and pencil. "Every visitor to the park can get a kit," said Ranger Mark. Lily smiled. She wanted a green kit for her own notebook. "Which key words do you like best?" asked Ranger Mark. "I like frog and leaves, because I can see them in my mind," said May.
